## February 2025: Ukraine minerals, Putin summit talk, and the DECLAS push

With Trump back in the [[white-house|White House]] in February 2025, residents and workers in Washington, D.C. appeared anxious about their legal exposure after a campaign built around a message of "retribution" against those he believed wronged him during the Biden years; Google search-trend data showed searches for "criminal defense lawyer" soaring in the capital in January, nearly five times higher than in Utah, the state with the second-most such searches.[{N}]

Trump inaugurated an official White House channel on [[rumble|Rumble]], the video platform and cloud services provider, adding the administration to the company's expanding portfolio of content providers.[{N}] Rumble chief executive [[chris-pavlovski|Chris Pavlovski]] reported that the first briefing carried on the platform peaked around 55,000 live viewers against roughly 22,000 on YouTube.[{N}]

On Ukraine, Trump dispatched Treasury Secretary [[scott-bessent|Scott Bessent]] to Kyiv — the first senior administration official to visit — a day after Russia released an American prisoner, which Trump called a positive signal for cease-fire talks.[{N}] He wrote on Truth Social that "this war must and will end soon — too much death and destruction," and complained that the United States had spent billions of dollars "with too little to show" for it.[{N}] Trump claimed Kiev had agreed to relinquish $500 billion worth of rare-earth minerals to compensate for aid provided under [[joe-biden|Joe Biden]], a claim contested by [[denis-pushilin|Denis Pushilin]] of the [[donetsk-peoples-republic|Donetsk People's Republic]], who said most of the lithium and titanium lies in Russian-held Donbass.[{N}]

Trump named [[saudi-arabia|Saudi Arabia]] as the likely host of his first meeting with Russian President [[vladimir-putin|Vladimir Putin]] of his second term, telling journalists in the Oval Office, "The first time we'll meet in Saudi Arabia, see if we get something done," and indicating several meetings could follow.[{N}] He noted that both leaders know Crown Prince [[mohammed-bin-salman|Mohammed bin Salman]] and that the kingdom could be "a very good place to meet."[{N}] Badlands commentary also noted that Trump had [[karoline-leavitt|Karoline Leavitt]] tell the press pool that he and [[king-abdullah-ii|King Abdullah]] differed on how to handle Gaza, and that he had asked Arab states to return with a better proposal.[{N}]

On Tuesday, February 11, 2025, Trump signed an executive order formally requiring federal agencies to cooperate with [[elon-musk|Elon Musk]] and the [[doge|Department of Government Efficiency]]; hundreds of [[small-business-administration|Small Business Administration]] employees received termination notices within hours.[{N}] North Korean state media, via the [[korean-central-news-agency|Korean Central News Agency]], denounced his proposal to take over Gaza and relocate Palestinians as bluster, accusing Washington of robbery and criticizing calls to take the Panama Canal and Greenland and to rename the Gulf of Mexico the "Gulf of America."[{N}]

Also in February 2025, Musk's [[x-corp|X]] agreed to pay about $10 million to settle the lawsuit Trump had filed in 2021 over his deplatforming after the January 6, 2021 Capitol riot, making X the second social-media platform to settle such litigation.[{N}]

## February 2025: DOGE firings, Tesla threats, and the X settlement

On Tuesday, February 11, 2025, President [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] signed an executive order formally forcing federal agencies to cooperate with Musk and his [[doge|Department of Government Efficiency]] takeover of the federal bureaucracy.[{N}] Just hours later, a few hundred [[small-business-administration|Small Business Administration]] employees received emails with formal termination notices; reporting indicated employees had received similar notices the previous Friday, been told on Monday the notices were a mistake, and then been officially cut on Tuesday, prompting one source to say they were "jerked around like this for the sake of EO choreography."[{N}] Musk stood by the firings, arguing, "If the bureaucracy is in charge, then what meaning does democracy actually have? It does not match the will of the people, so it's just something we've got to fix."[{N}]

Hostility toward Musk translated into threats against [[tesla|Tesla]] owners. In Arcata, California, four Tesla owners reported threatening notes left on their vehicles in early February 2025, allegedly by a group calling itself [[students-against-nazi-extremism|Students Against Nazi Extremism]]; at least one note was wrapped around a brick, and an accompanying manifesto called Musk "an overt Nazi with a history of fascist, racist, misogynist and criminal behavior."[{N}] A Tesla dealership in Colorado was targeted by vandals and arsonists three times in the same period.[{N}] Badlands commentary faulted years of institutional anti-Trump rhetoric for fueling such crimes and singled out Representative [[jamie-raskin|Jamie Raskin]] for remarks the hosts read as xenophobic toward a successful legal immigrant and as encouragement to violence.[{N}]

In the same month, Musk's [[x-corp|X]] agreed to pay about $10 million to settle the lawsuit Trump filed in 2021 against the company — then Twitter — and its chief executive at the time, [[jack-dorsey|Jack Dorsey]], over Trump's deplatforming following the January 6, 2021 Capitol riot.[{N}] Musk had reinstated Trump on the platform in November 2022.[{N}] Trump's team weighed letting the suit fizzle out, citing Musk's proximity to the president and the $250 million he spent to help elect him, but proceeded with the settlement anyway.[{N}]

## February 2025: Executive order and the SBA firings

On Tuesday, February 11, 2025, President [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] signed an executive order formally forcing federal agencies to cooperate with [[elon-musk|Elon Musk]] and the Department of Government Efficiency's takeover of the federal government.[{N}] Employees at the [[small-business-administration|Small Business Administration]] began being fired before the ink was dry: within hours a few hundred SBA staff received emails with formal termination notices.[{N}] People involved with the agency said employees had received similar notices the previous Friday, were told on Monday that the notices were a mistake, and were then officially cut on Tuesday — behavior one source described as jerking people around "for the sake of EO choreography."[{N}]

Musk defended the cuts, asking, "If the bureaucracy is in charge, then what meaning does democracy actually have?" and arguing that entrenched bureaucracy "does not match the will of the people."[{N}] Critics questioned whether firing hundreds of federal employees really reflected the will of the people; Badlands hosts answered emphatically that it did.[{N}] Other Badlands commentary cautioned against "toxic positivity" in the movement, arguing that questioning leadership is a feature rather than a bug and that Trump and Musk want a mandate rather than fealty.[{N}]
scott-bessent:
## February 2025: Kyiv mission

In February 2025 Bessent was expected to become the first senior [[donald-trump|Trump]] administration official to visit Ukraine, traveling to Kyiv a day after Russia released an American prisoner in a development Trump called a positive signal for cease-fire talks.[{N}] The trip came amid anxiety in Kyiv and among American allies over whether U.S. support for the Ukrainian war effort would be maintained.[{N}]

The administration had already sought an arrangement for the United States to secure rights to Ukrainian natural resources, including rare earth minerals, as a guarantee for further assistance.[{N}] Trump wrote on Truth Social that he was sending Bessent because "this war must and will end soon — too much death and destruction," and that the visit would address American assistance, which he said had cost billions "with too little to show" for it.[{N}] Trump summarized the mission bluntly: "Treasury's Bessent is going to Ukraine to make sure we get money back."[{N}] Ukrainian President [[volodymyr-zelensky|Volodymyr Zelensky]] welcomed the visit, saying, "We are already prepared for meetings with representatives of the United States — negotiations will begin soon."[{N}]

## February 2025: The minerals-for-aid offer

In February 2025 Zelensky welcomed the announced visit of U.S. Treasury Secretary [[scott-bessent|Scott Bessent]] to Kyiv, saying in an evening address, "We are already prepared for meetings with representatives of the United States — negotiations will begin soon."[{N}] The visit came amid anxiety in Kyiv over whether American support for the war effort would continue under [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]].[{N}]

Zelensky offered the United States privileged access to Ukrainian natural resources to incentivize continued military assistance, and Trump claimed Kiev had agreed to relinquish $500 billion worth of rare-earth minerals to compensate for aid previously provided under [[joe-biden|Joe Biden]].[{N}] Ukraine's backers argued the country could supply trillions of dollars' worth of raw materials, including coal, iron ore, lithium, titanium, graphite and uranium.[{N}] [[denis-pushilin|Denis Pushilin]], head of the [[donetsk-peoples-republic|Donetsk People's Republic]], countered that the majority of the reserves Zelensky's team was offering lie in the Donbass, under territory now controlled by Russia, saying, "Most of the lithium and titanium is within our territory, which has already been liberated."[{N}]

## February 2025: DECLAS task force

In February 2025 Luna, a Florida Republican and member of the [[house-freedom-caucus|House Freedom Caucus]] first elected in 2022, was tasked with revisiting "federal secrets" surrounding the assassinations of [[john-f-kennedy|John F. Kennedy]] and [[martin-luther-king-jr|Martin Luther King Jr.]], as well as [[jeffrey-epstein|Jeffrey Epstein]]'s so-called "client list."[{N}] She had repeatedly pushed for transparency in the federal government, including on unidentified flying objects, the origins of COVID-19, and the September 11 attacks — all of which were slated to fall within her task force's remit.[{N}] Press coverage placed her among a class of GOP insurgents and [[donald-trump|Trump]] loyalists who had recently floated a bill to put Trump's face on Mount Rushmore.[{N}]

Profiles of the 35-year-old lawmaker noted six years of military service in the Air Force and Oregon Air National Guard, work as a cocktail waitress at a gentlemen's club and as a swimsuit model for publications including Liberty Belles, and a following built as an Instagram influencer before she pivoted into far-right politics.[{N}]

Badlands host [[jon-herold|Jon Herold]] was sharply skeptical of the DECLAS committee, arguing that the movement should "stop taking steps backward for the sake of waking up the normies" and questioning whether Luna was attempting to co-opt declassification from Trump by implying the task force existed so bad actors could not block release.[{N}] He noted that she had never advocated for or even mentioned declassification of the JFK files before that week, apart from thanking Trump for delivering on his promise to do so.[{N}]

## February 2025: Official White House channel

In February 2025 Rumble Inc. (NASDAQ: RUM), then a $2.73 billion market cap video platform and cloud services provider, announced the inauguration of an official [[white-house|White House]] channel by President [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]], adding the administration to the company's expanding portfolio of content providers.[{N}] The company's stock had returned 118% over the preceding six months, and the partnership was expected to increase Rumble's visibility and user base as it positioned itself as independent infrastructure supporting a free and open internet.[{N}]

Rumble chief executive [[chris-pavlovski|Chris Pavlovski]] occupied the "new media seat" in the White House briefing room that Monday and was given the first question.[{N}] He later reported that, according to StreamsCharts, YouTube peaked at around 22,000 live viewers while Rumble peaked at around 55,000 live viewers for the White House press briefing with [[karoline-leavitt|Karoline Leavitt]].[{N}] [[badlands-media|Badlands Media]] carried its own special coverage of the briefing and post-briefing commentary on the platform.[{N}]

## February 2025: FEMA clawback

In February 2025 Homeland Security Secretary Noem announced that the [[donald-trump|Trump]] administration had retrieved $59 million that the [[fema|Federal Emergency Management Agency]] had allocated the previous week to house illegal aliens in New York City hotels.[{N}] "I have clawed back the full payment that FEMA deep state activists unilaterally gave to NYC migrant hotels," she wrote on X.[{N}]

Noem said FEMA had been funding the Roosevelt Hotel, which she described as serving as a [[tren-de-aragua|Tren de Aragua]] base of operations and as housing the killer of [[laken-riley|Laken Riley]] — a reference to [[jose-antonio-ibarra|Jose Antonio Ibarra]], an illegal alien from Venezuela found guilty in November of murdering the Georgia nursing student.[{N}] "Mark my words," she added, "there will not be a single penny spent that goes against the interest and safety of the American people."[{N}]

## February 2025: Settlement of the Trump deplatforming suit

In February 2025 [[elon-musk|Elon Musk]]'s X agreed to pay about $10 million to settle a lawsuit that [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] had brought against the company and its former chief executive, making X the second social-media platform to settle litigation Trump filed after being deplatformed over his role in the January 6, 2021 riot at the U.S. Capitol.[{N}] Trump and other plaintiffs filed the suit in 2021 against the company, then called Twitter, and its chief executive at the time, [[jack-dorsey|Jack Dorsey]].[{N}] Musk reinstated Trump on the platform in November 2022.[{N}]

Trump's team considered letting the lawsuit fizzle out, citing Musk's proximity to the president and the $250 million he spent to help elect him, but ultimately moved forward with the settlement despite the two men's close relationship; a spokesman for X did not respond to requests for comment.[{N}]

## February 2025: Condemnation of the Gaza takeover proposal

On Wednesday, February 12, 2025, North Korean state media denounced U.S. President [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]]'s proposal to take over Gaza and relocate Palestinians as bluster, accusing Washington of robbery.[{N}] A commentary carried by the [[korean-central-news-agency|Korean Central News Agency]] said the slim hopes of Palestinians for safety and peace were being crushed by the proposal, and declared that "the world is now boiling like a porridge pot over the U.S.' bombshell declaration" — without naming Trump directly.[{N}] The commentary also criticized calls to take over the Panama Canal and Greenland and the decision to rename the "Gulf of Mexico" the "Gulf of America," urging that "the U.S. should awaken from its anachronistic daydream and stop at once the act of encroaching upon the dignity and sovereignty of other countries and nations," and calling the United States a "ferocious robber" and an "accomplice" to Israel's actions in Gaza.[{N}]

Badlands commentary read the omission of Trump's name as a deliberate signal that Kim was targeting neoconservatives in Trump's orbit rather than the president himself, likening the rhetoric to professional-wrestling heel work even as Trump spoke fondly of their friendship and of wanting to catch up by phone.[{N}]

## February 2025: Remarks on Elon Musk

In February 2025 Raskin drew criticism from Badlands commentators over remarks about [[elon-musk|Elon Musk]] made amid a wave of threats and vandalism directed at [[tesla|Tesla]] owners and dealerships, including notes left on vehicles in Arcata, California by a group calling itself [[students-against-nazi-extremism|Students Against Nazi Extremism]].[{N}] The hosts argued that Raskin was being overtly xenophobic about a successful legal immigrant and that his rhetoric amounted to dog-whistling supporters toward further acts of violence against Tesla and possibly Musk himself; they also described him as appearing demoralized and defeated in the clip in question.[{N}]
